I am hoping to dip my toe into all aspects of the wiki including feedback, but I do wish to see how all the forums work and get a feel for the community to start off with. As for the Question of the month, I've always been obsessed with space, as I'm sure most of you do as well, I often get lost in how small we are. But frankly, I find it very humbling.

item.title: SCP Idea - Lost World
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article + Tale

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, Exploration and Tale connected to it.

Elevator Pitch: Mansion in which pianist remains is placed 2 miles East in Allegheny National Forest. Anomalous pianist creates world and story of it's fall in his music. People that will hear his music hallucinate through it's whole story being able to hear and see everything, but not being able to interact with that world. People under influence will feel like the story continues for hours while in normal time it's only about 5 minutes long. After seeing it's whole story, influenced individuals show symptoms of extreme depression and inability to die of old age as they are "already dead inside".

Central Narrative: Everything occurs in mansion build 2 miles East in Allegheny National Forest. Previously mentioned anomalous pianist plays a song with length of 4 minutes and 56 seconds, but for influenced person it's like hours. Pianist shows them all tragedies of "lost world". Everyone who sees the story became extremely depressed and unable to talk about it to the point where influenced individuals commit suicide. People influenced by this SCP are empty. They are alive, but they barely eat, drink or sleep and a they do is look nowhere. People that saw the story are unable to die of old age as they are "already dead inside". Only one D-Class individual was able to keep part of his sanity and as ex writer, he was able to write just a portion of what he saw as a tale. D-Class few weeks after dies by stabbing his own throat with pen, he was given to write the rest of story.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I waned to focus on emotional pressure on reader and I just waned to write what and how I feel.

Additional Notes:
I didn't wrote what the story contains for purpose to keep it hidden for now.

item.title: The Petrifying Statue
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Traditional structure of containment procedures followed by description.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This is a statue crafted by AWCY and placed in a public place.
  • When no humans are stood close to it, it remains a statue but when a human is stood close to it, they will be attacked.
  • If they cannot escape, they are killed by an unknown process which petrifies their internal organs and fluids.
  • Humans can avoid the attack by breaking up their human form with exterior objects and costumes.

Central Narrative: It is a traditional article, which is further expanding the anomalous object count which the group is responsible for.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A statue which requires humans to be present for its anomalous properties to manifest, but this manifestation can be worked around by various means, protecting said person from a horrible death where their insides are solidified.

item.title: Re: Blood Storm
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Let's do this…

A storm that appears once every 4 years in a completely random location on Earth. The rain is red and feels like blood and if touched with bare skin it will turn you into a mindless zombie with increased speed and strength. It is not possible to convert people back to normal.

So why is it random? Why does it make people turn into zombies? Why do the zombies have increased speed and strength? It's not possible to convert people back to normal? So even SCP-500 can't heal them? I have so many questions.

This SCP is usually the size of the state of Texas. It will appear on a random day after 4 years in a random location at a random time which makes it much harder to tell if the storm is abroad. The first hour of the storm will appear as just cloudy but after the hour is over, the rain will begin to pour. During the first hour, civilians in the range of the storm will be warned of the storm via EAS on television, radio, and cell phone. Anyone not taking cover will be detained by arriving MTF agents. Aggression towards MTF agents will be met with lethal force. The storm will usually last between 16 to 28 hours and once its over, all civilians in the area must be given amnestics to forget about the past hours of the storm. Anyone lost during the event must be given a cover story as to why they are gone.

What's the narrative? It sounds like you only gave me the containment procedures.

During the most recent event, a man created a journal explaining his experience of the storm and everything that happens while the MTF guard the streets to keep people safe.

Okay, so I believe this is the narrative. Mind going into a bit more detail?

Overall Thoughts: You barely went into description of the Narrative. All I know is the SCP containment procedures and that a man writing down his experiences with the Foundation and said SCP. I suggest you give the narrative much more detail and thought. I also feel that the anomaly itself makes very little sense. Why zombies? Why blood? Why do the zombies have enhanced psychical abilities? I feel like more thought needs to be put into this stuff. It sounds like you put a bunch of words into a blender and hoped for the best.

You can contact a butterfly to help you out or go to the IRC to get another reviewer. Both have a ton of experience.

- Close

item.title: Re: The Knife (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.content:encoded:
So I guess my main concern is that you’re raising a lot of questions, but you don’t seem to bother answering any of them. The article’s all about this mysterious cult that has strange chanting, which I’d love to learn about but I wouldn’t want to wonder about. The same goes for the coordinates on the knife, it feels like this island should mean something but it’s never mentioned again. It certainly feels like you’ve thought about this, but I don’t feel like I’m getting the full picture.

A few more unrelated notes. Murderous knives have kind of been done already. I’d be interested in seeing some other weapon though, maybe a spear or an axe or a metal spike. Really depends what kind of feel you’re going for, I just think some other weapon would let this stand out more. Also, the idea of anyone seeing the knife wielded dying instantly is just unnecessary. There’s a difference between making something more dangerous and making it scary.

Overall, I like the cult vibe. If I knew more about the background of this weapon I think it’d be really interesting. Just make sure to look through your powers again and make sure you really need them all. Sometimes you can get too distracted thinking about what the SCP could do that you forget what it needs to do.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Knife (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)

item.title: Re: The Sanctum
item.content:encoded:
Thx for the feedback it's really helpful and appreciated.

In terms of how the Sanctum has remained hidden, it's because they acted in secrecy on par with the foundation, the Star of Bethlehem (SOB) guiding them to anomalies before the foundation can get to them. Another main reason is because of the heavy self-isolation the Sanctum has, it didn't know the foundation existed. It wasn't until the foundation became fully efficient that they were able to track and find anomalies just as fast as the Sanctum and the two eventually clashed leading to the vanishing agents, and later the Sanctum's discovery.

In terms of relations with other GoI, the Sanctum worked in heavy secrecy and mainly operated inside of Italy and Europe so its existence is almost unknown to the whole world aside from the Foundation when it's uncovered. But the foundation does find members of the Serpent's Hand contained within the prison, but the Serpent's hand are unaware of who was responsible.

item.title: Re: A problem with alot of scp articles.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-914 is an older writing (from series 1), and primarily since a lot of nostalgia surrounds it, it's less likely to be edited.
To explain why some information is censored (or "redacted" as many it's often called), that's actually to serve as a narrative ( someone off-site mentioned that the lore is supposed to mean that the reader is supossedly accessing confidential information, and thus is their own character).
Try to read some newer SCP's and see if there's any difference, as newer entries tend to have a different feel to them. They may be written with less common language.
